Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport/identity authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the originating state's designated competent authority; consular legalization by the consulate of Canada if originating state is not party to the Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of existence / certificate of good standing of any corporate shareholder or beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry authority of the corporate shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization in the country of issuance, followed by certified translation into French or English if not already in one of those languages

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certificate of incumbency / directory of officers and directors for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary and notary public in the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, as applicable, with sworn French/English translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the Quebec incorporation agent and registered office provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, then reviewed by a Quebec notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Consent to act as director (Quebec Business Corporations Act prescribed form) signed by each initial director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Individual director and Quebec stipulating notary or recognized commissioner for oaths
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Local notarization; apostille/consular legalization only where the director signs outside Canada

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all applicants, directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against FINTRAC, OFAC (SDN and sectoral lists), United Nations Security Council consolidated lists, Canadian emergency economic sanctions (Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, S.C. 1990, c. 32), and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2017, c. 21. PEP review includes senior Federal/Provincial officials, foreign PEPs, and close associates/family members; enhanced due diligence applies to wire transfers, politically exposed persons, and legal persons based in high-risk jurisdictions. A risk-based questionnaire and beneficial-ownership chain documentation must be completed before any corporate cipher or subscription service is activated.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire d'entreprises du Québec (REQ) – 'Registre des entreprises' and the Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre, Quebec name-reservation portal (application via REQ web services or third-party NUANS accredited service)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name of a Quebec business corporation must comply with the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11). The corporate name may be in French exclusively or comprised of a French version and an English version; if only one version is adopted, it must be French. Name tokens must use Latin alphabet characters, and any non-French name must be accompanied by a French transliteration or a French-form version. The REQ requires an official NUANS/REQ name report to demonstrate that the proposed name is linguistically acceptable, not confusing with existing enterprises, and does not include prohibited terms. Numerals, punctuation, and distinctive elements are restricted to avoid misleading designations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, banker, banking, trust, insurance/assurance, broker, exchange, and any regulated financial-services token unless the corporation obtains prior ministerial/regulator approval
University, college, institute, professional, engineer/ingénieur, lawyer/avocat, physician/médecin, geologist, and other regulated professional terms requiring licence or title consent
Crown, federal, incorporated, corporation, registred, not-for-profit, or any token suggesting governmental sponsorship or misleading status
Terms implying charitable, public-security, law-enforcement, or military affiliation without express authorization
Obscene, scandalous, discriminatory, or territorially misleading names (e.g., 'Quebec' can be used only in a geographically accurate and non-flagrant context)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected by the REQ, the applicant may file a written administrative-review request within 30 days of the refusal, restating the proposed name and providing a new NUANS/REQ search report if the search has lapsed. The REQ will issue a written reason. If the refusal is confirmed, the applicant may apply to the Court of Québec (Civil Chamber, judicial review) or, for questions of linguistic justice, appeal to the Tribunal administratif du Québec; all submissions must be in French. A rejected name may be submitted in modified form, adding new distinctive tokens, a French legal form suffix, or a corporate number identifier, without losing the original priority if the amended name remains substantially distinct and is supported by a valid current NUANS/REQ report.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible for a low-risk design-subscription business. A Quebec business corporation must maintain a registered office in Quebec at an identifiable physical street address where process, corporate records, and ministerial notices can be served. A licensed virtual-office provider with a physical reception address, mail-holding service, and a resident director/agent satisfies the registry requirement. The regulator may require disclosure in the enterprise register that the establishment is administrative only. For GST/QST registration purposes, virtual offices are accepted, but the corporation must have at least one executive/operational decision-maker located in Canada; a purely offshore sole shareholder with no Canadian presence and no resident agent creates heightened substance risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low ~ 10% annualized probability of an unannounced verification visit by the Registraire des entreprises or Revenu Québec for the first fiscal year, rising to 20-30% if the registered office is a high-density shared workspace or if filings contain inconsistencies. Since the business has no statutory licence, inspections focus on documentary evidence of address and control, not physical premises.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. S-31.1, including sections 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 18, 19 and 20 concerning incorporation, articles, registered office, directors and share structure; Regulation respecting legal person publicity, CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 2.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), Ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Constitution of a Business Corporation, filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, generally using REQ form RE-300 or the applicable online incorporation service.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies. Shares may be issued for consideration determined by the corporation and authorized by the board. Quebec does not require a statutory incorporation escrow account. The corporation must maintain proper corporate records and evidence of consideration received for issued shares.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation accept and approve the subscription by the incorporator or subscriber for the number and class of shares specified in the subscription agreement, for the stated consideration, and that the shares be issued as fully paid upon receipt of that consideration. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation be established at the Quebec address stated in the incorporation records. RESOLVED, that the following persons be appointed as officers: [name], President; [name], Secretary; and [name], Treasurer, each to serve until replacement or resignation. RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to complete all registry, banking, tax, insurance and operational filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Entity Form, Name and Corporate Structure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online services and Corporations Canada name-search resources where applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm whether the entity will be incorporated under the Quebec Business Corporations Act or federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act and extra-provincially registered in Quebec. Select a compliant corporate name or use a numbered corporation. Verify French-language and trademark considerations, shareholder classes, authorized share terms, registered office, directors and officers.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name or numbered-corporation request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise the name, share provisions or personal-information disclosures and resubmit. For a name objection, provide supporting consent, adopt a numbered name or file a new name request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and File Articles of Constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online filing portal or REQ service counter.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the articles of constitution, identify the registered office, incorporator, directors and share provisions, and submit the prescribed filing fee. Quebec generally does not require notarization for standard electronic incorporation documents. Any foreign-language supporting document should be accompanied by an acceptable French translation where requested.
required_dossiers: Government identification and authorization for the filer
French translations of non-French supporting documents, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the REQ query within the stated deadline, correct rejected fields, replace a non-compliant name or attach missing evidence. Refile electronically and retain the submission receipt.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Constituting Documents and Quebec Enterprise Identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the certificate or confirmation of constitution, corporate number, current enterprise registration extract and filed articles. Verify the legal name, registered office, directors, officers, activity codes and beneficial-owner disclosures. Correct any registry error promptly through an amendment filing.
required_dossiers: Corporate number and Québec enterprise number (NEQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File an amendment, correction or update with the REQ and provide documentary support. If an administrative decision is disputed, use the applicable review or court procedure under Quebec enterprise-register legislation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Organizational Meeting and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's board of directors and shareholders; corporate records office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the organizational resolutions, approve the registered office, appoint officers, approve banking authority, issue shares against documented consideration, adopt signing authorities and establish accounting and records procedures. No notarization is normally required, but resolutions and subscription documents must be signed and retained in the minute book.
required_dossiers: Share certificate or electronic share register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Ratify defective acts by subsequent board or shareholder resolutions, correct the securities register and amend inaccurate corporate records. Obtain legal advice before curing an invalid share issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Tax, Payroll and Commercial Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency; Revenu Québec; Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail; applicable financial institution.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a CRA business number and required corporate income-tax, GST/HST and payroll accounts. Register for Quebec sales tax where applicable and assess QST registration based on taxable supplies and small-supplier rules. Register with CNESST where Quebec employees or covered workers require it. Open a corporate bank account and implement bookkeeping controls.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct account applications, provide requested identity or activity evidence, and submit outstanding returns or elections. Apply for voluntary disclosures or penalty relief only where statutory eligibility is satisfied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec, Canada Revenue Agency, Revenu Québec and the corporation's directors.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Track the annual update declaration, annual corporate returns, tax filings, payroll remittances, GST/HST and QST filings, beneficial-owner updates, corporate-record maintenance and director approvals. Update the REQ within the prescribed period after changes to address, directors, officers, activities or beneficial ownership.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File overdue returns and amendments, pay applicable late fees and interest, and respond to compliance notices. Restore or regularize the corporation before entering material contracts if its registry status is impaired.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for a digital UI/UX design subscription agency. Municipal authorities and the Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs may apply to premises or activities that create regulated impacts.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific manufacturing or industrial operating licence is ordinarily required for ISIC 7410 digital design services. Municipal occupancy, zoning or business-permit requirements must be checked for the selected premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs du Québec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt or not applicable for office-based digital design and subscription services, subject to site-specific activities and premises.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No routine wastewater, VOC or industrial-emissions permit is normally triggered by ordinary office operations. The corporation must manage hazardous materials, electronic waste, waste disposal and any construction or alteration impacts in accordance with applicable Quebec environmental and municipal requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No industrial civil-defence clearance is ordinarily required. The premises must comply with municipal building, zoning and occupancy rules, the Quebec Building Code and applicable fire-safety requirements. Fire protection systems, emergency exits, occupant loads and structural alterations may require municipal or fire-service approval. Employers must comply with occupational-health and safety requirements administered by CNESST, including workplace risk prevention and required incident reporting.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — My Business Account / Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec — Mon dossier d'entreprise (CléNuméro) for QST accounts
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first register for a federal Business Number (BN) with the CRA using Business Registration Online or Form RC1; the GST/HST account is opened under the same BN. For Quebec-only taxable supplies, the entity must also register with Revenu Québec through the enterprise registration portal to obtain a QST registration number. Non-resident corporations are required to register if they carry on a taxable business in Canada or exceed the registration threshold; a Canadian agent or certified tax representative may be mandated; treaty-based permanent establishment analysis applies for income tax, but GST/QST registration is independent of income tax residence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Canadian-resident corporation taxed on worldwide income; non-resident corporation taxed only on Canadian-source income through permanent establishment rules; no general pass-through election exists for business corporations; Quebec corporate income tax applies to the same corporate person)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election is available in Canada; foreign entities cannot elect C-Corp or partnership character. Hybrid mismatch rules (Income Tax Act s.18.6 and s.37.1) may recharacterize payouts. Specific elections include s.216 election for non-residents deriving Canadian rental/real-property income, s.219 branch-profit deemed-dividend election, and GST/HST voluntary registration under s.240 ETA for business-starting registrants; Revenu Québec administers analogous QST elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-added type dual GST/HST and QST (Quebec Sales Tax) regime
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold on worldwide taxable revenues for GST/HST and QST; for non-resident suppliers of digital services, simplified mandatory registration applies when quarterly taxable supplies to Canadian consumers exceed CAD 30,000; voluntary registration available below threshold where a commercial activity exists
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API mandate is currently in force in Quebec/Canada. Electronic invoices are accepted where they sufficiently state taxable supplies, GST/HST and QST amounts, vendor registration numbers, and currency conversion. Both CRA and Revenu Québec require retention of electronic books and records; federal procurement and interoperability standards align with Peppol BIS 3.0; invoice data generated through Stripe Billing or Wise must be mapped to the statutory invoice content rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, zero-rating applies where tangible personal property is exported in a supply to a non-resident and the supplier maintains evidence of exportation within statutory timelines. For services, a supply to a non-resident is 0%-rated under ETA s.7(1), Part V, Schedule VI unless it falls within excepted services performed in Canada (e.g., advisory/consulting, management, scientific or technical services). UI/UX subscription design should be documented as a supply of intangible personal property, rights of use, or non-resident-directed digital services rather than Canadian-site advisory work, and the recipient’s non-resident status must be evidenced (e.g., W-8 or foreign certificate of residency).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A or electronic export reporting; required for goods exceeding CAD 2,000 or listed controlled goods)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Inward Remittance Certificate or supporting bank confirmation of cross-border payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may deny zero-rated treatment and proportionally claw back input tax credits where export evidence is deficient. Penalties include 10% misrepresentation penalty or 50% gross-negligence penalty under s.285 ETA, interest on unremitted tax, and criminal prosecution for wilful evasion (ETA s.341(2)); QST penalties mirror GST/HST and are imposed by Revenu Québec. Retrospective reassessments may also trigger Canadian transfer-pricing and BEPS-linked income tax adjustments that, in turn, invalidate prior zero-rating positions and expose the registrant to treaty anti-abuse scrutiny.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full capital account convertibility under the Bank of Canada Act and Exchange Control Regulations. Current account transactions, including profit remittances, dividends, interest, and royalties to foreign shareholders, face no convertibility restrictions when executed through authorized foreign exchange dealers. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal and primarily limited to tax compliance, beneficial ownership verification, and anti-money laundering reporting requirements. All FX transactions exceeding CAD 10,000 must be reported to the Bank of Canada via licensed dealers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds is required under Canadian law. Exporters may retain foreign exchange proceeds or convert them to CAD at prevailing market rates through authorized dealers. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation of export receipts. Conversion ratios are market-driven. However, all FX transactions must be reported to the Bank of Canada if exceeding CAD 10,000, and non-reporting may trigger regulatory scrutiny.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for licensed fintech platforms such as Wise and Stripe Billing for cross-border payments and liquidity management. Legal constraints include mandatory registration with FINTRAC for AML compliance, use of bank-sponsored payment rails, and adherence to Canadian Payment Services Act requirements. Offshore digital EMIs must partner with Canadian chartered banks for full regulatory integration and operational approval.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote corporate account opening is permitted for low-risk entities with digital KYC verification through licensed providers. Directors or authorized signers may be required to complete video interviews or in-person verification for enhanced due diligence, particularly for first-time clients or high-volume transaction profiles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate registry extract, shareholder agreements, and certified proof of ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) including passports and proof of address
Source of funds and source of wealth documentation, transaction history, legal opinions confirming legitimacy, and beneficial ownership declarations

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from foreign clients or investors must utilize SWIFT wire transfers with purpose code 'Design Services' or 'Professional Fees'. Verification requires matching client identification, invoice details, and beneficial ownership confirmation. All transactions processed through Canadian chartered banks or licensed fintech with bank sponsorship, with full AML and tax documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for subscriptions or services utilize SWIFT MT103 with appropriate purpose codes. For trade settlements, Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) may be utilized through correspondent banks. All disbursements require prior approval and comprehensive documentation to comply with export controls and AML regulations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Currency swaps for multi-currency liquidity management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) to the Registraire des entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation; must be filed every 12 months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 10–100 per month; persistent non-filing beyond 2 years triggers administrative dissolution and strike-off from the enterprise register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end (mandatory for all active corporations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty equal to 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; repeat late filings incur 10% base penalty; criminal prosecution possible for chronic non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec CO-17 Corporate Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; returns are filed concurrently with federal T2
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month; administrative collection measures including garnishment and property seizure after continued default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST Return and Remittance (if taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due no later than 3 months after the fiscal year-end for annual filers; instalment requirements apply for higher net tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Compound interest on late remittance at prescribed CRA rates; failure to file penalty of 5% plus 1% per month on unpaid amount; prosecution for wilful evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) Annual Review and Update Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors minute book; subject to inspection by the Registraire des entreprises and law enforcement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Mandatory annual review at each fiscal year-end; immediate update within 15 days upon any change in significant control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors and officers liable to personal fines up to CAD 5,000 for failure to maintain or update the ISC register; shareholder inspection rights may be suspended

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Quebec Business Corporations Act does not require an audit for non-distributing corporations unless shareholders holding at least 5% of issued shares demand one; public or distributing corporations must appoint an external auditor at each annual meeting
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for publicly accountable enterprises; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for private corporations under the Quebec CPA Canada Handbook

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every Quebec business corporation must maintain a current register of individuals with significant control, reviewed at fiscal year-end and updated within 15 days of any shareholding or control change; the Registraire des entreprises may inspect the register under confidentiality safeguards and non-disclosure agreements
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150–400 per year for a commercial registered office or corporate agent in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200–5,000 per year for a small private Quebec business corporation with typical online subscription revenue
